content:
Facts: Three daughters and their mother, co-heirs of deceased father, disputed estate division comprising two residential units (converted from rural building with costs borne partially by mother and one daughter) and agricultural land; one daughter sought assignment of entire property; another daughter claimed credit for renovation expenses initially filed belatedly as counterclaim then re-filed in separate joined proceedings; plaintiff claimed occupancy compensation and alleged misappropriation of estate assets.
Legal Framework: Articles 718, 720, 724-727 Italian Civil Code (estate division in kind; inconvenient divisibility; credits toward joint ownership); Art. 540(2) (spousal habitation right on family home); Arts. 167, 273 Italian Code of Civil Procedure (belated counterclaims; joinder of proceedings); Art. 2646 (transcription requirements).
Interpretive Issues: Whether division in kind feasible when estate comprises heterogeneous assets (residential properties and agricultural land) requiring disproportionate monetary adjustments; admissibility of credit claim for renovation expenses filed belatedly as counterclaim then re-submitted in separate proceedings; calculation of shares when one residential unit partially built on land exclusively owned by co-heir; scope of spousal habitation right on converted multi-family dwelling; allocation of burden of proof for co-heir's alleged contributions to renovation costs and appropriation of deceased's funds.
Principles Applied: Estate inconveniently divisible when monetary adjustments disproportionately high relative to asset values, effectively denying division in kind objective. Assignment to single heir permitted under Art. 720 when no other co-heir requests allocation. Spousal habitation right under Art. 540(2) attaches only to portion constituting original family dwelling, not subsequently created residential units from ancillary structures. Belated counterclaim inadmissible under Art. 167 but validly re-proposed in separate proceedings; simultaneous pendency before same court resolved by joinder under Art. 273, consolidating claims for single ruling. Co-heir claiming renovation expense credit bears proof burden; probabilistic judgment sufficient when documentary evidence incomplete but corroborated by witness testimony regarding payment sources. Credit for improvements to joint property deducted from assignee's payment obligation under Arts. 724-725. Assets built on land exclusively owned by co-heir excluded from divisible estate; cadastral regularization required. Estate valuation considers current market values; portion values must reflect encumbrances (habitation rights valued using actuarial tables based on usufructuary's age). Adjustment debts constitute value debts requiring revaluation and interest from succession opening. Court-appointed expert costs allocated proportionally: per inheritance shares for division operations; equally among defeated parties for contested claims.
